Hey Stephanie / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're starting final pre-cutover checks for the Acme private VPC; before we flip any circuits we wanted one short alignment readout on two items that came up during our staging test:

1) Control-plane adjacency: we saw a ~250ms control plane retry when the control-plane pod moved between racks (staging). Can you confirm your recommended control-plane HA pattern (active/active vs active/standby) and whether the published reference diagram covers the rack-level cross-connects we just received?

2) Data-plane stitching: our ops team flagged an egress hairpin when tenant egress uses the on-prem NAT vs the cloud-proxy. Do you have an explicit failover order and prefix ownership table we can consume for routing rules?

Attached: our staging tcpdump and a short note from netops. Would appreciate a 30–45 min readout today or tomorrow to close these off before cutover.

Tom
Infrastructure lead, Acme Commerce

Subject: Re: Private VPC handoff — quick pre-cutover alignment

Tom — thanks for the clear notes and the captures. High level answers up front, then specifics below:

- Control-plane: we recommend active/active across two control-plane pods in different racks with BGP peering for keepalive and a thin L3 anycast for the control-plane VIP. That pattern avoids single-rack context switches and reduces retry windows.
- Data-plane egress: the failover order should be: 1) local on-prem NAT (preferred for latency), 2) site-level egress proxy (private proxy cluster), 3) cloud egress via Redwood transit (fallback). The prefix ownership table is attached in the controlplane-dataflow-annotated.pdf.

Questions / asks before we schedule readout:
- Can you confirm the topo for the two racks (names/IDs) that will host the control-plane pods? We need those for the cross-connect ports and to pre-seed ARP/BFD neighbors.
- Are there any egress ACLs on the on-prem NAT that would block the 10.16.0.0/12 internal prefixes?

I've attached our reference diagram (private-vpc-reference-diagram-v2.png) and a preliminary canary cutover checklist (canary-cutover-checklist.xlsx). Propose a 30-minute call today at 3pm PT — will loop in marissa and jonas for ops/observability items.

—Stephanie
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Tom Hastings <thastings@acme.com>, Acme Networking Team <netops@acme.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2029 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC handoff — quick pre-cutover alignment

Looping in a couple of ops items we saw in the staging run:

- Observability: during rack moves the control-plane metrics (leader election latency, kvcache reconnects) showed a short spike that correlated with a BFD session reset. Jonas — can you confirm whether BFD timers are still set to 300ms/3 (probe/interval) in our reference? If so we should lower the interval to 100ms for Acme's fabric to reduce detection jitter.
- KV cache warmup: when the control-plane moved we had a ~30–60s period where some requests hit fallback model variants because the KV cache didn't warm fast enough. We recommend pre-warming after any maintenance window with a scripted sweep (included in the checklist).

Tom — regarding your point on prefix ownership: our PDF lists the primary/secondary ASNs and the exact prefixes Redwood will announce from the on-prem tor uplinks. If your NAT has any outbound ACLs that drop private-to-private, that will cause the hairpin. If possible, allow 10.16.0.0/12 between the on-prem NAT and the proxy fabric.

Marissa
Senior Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: ops-kv-warmup.sh (script)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC handoff — quick pre-cutover alignment

Quick clarifications from the infra side:

- BFD: reference uses 300ms/3 by default; agree with Marissa that for Acme's fabric we should use 100ms/3 during cutover windows and revert afterwards. I'll add the change to the checklist as an explicit step (step 4).
- Control-plane VIP: we'll publish an anycast /32 with ECMP across the two racks; health will be L3/L4 probe + a session-level leader check. If a rack fails we will withdraw the route within the BGP convergence window — tested to ~800ms in our lab.
- Egress hairpin: to avoid hairpin the on-prem NAT must not SNAT internal prefixes to a public range for intra-tenant traffic. If that's unavoidable, we'll need a NAT exemption rule for the 10.16/12 block.

Jonas
Infra Lead | Redwood Inference

- NAT team confirmed they can add a NAT-exempt rule for 10.16.0.0/12 for intra-tenant flows; they'll also mirror the BFD timer change for the maintenance window.

Tom
